issues.title: Generic calendar suffix filtering includes disabled providers
issues.description: The getGenericCalendarSuffixes() method uses Object.keys(GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES) to iterate over all providers defined in the constant, including office365_calendar. However, getProviders() only returns ['google_calendar'], meaning Office365 is not actually enabled. This causes the subscription system to filter out Office365 calendar suffixes even when Office365 calendars shouldn't be processed at all. The filtering should only include suffixes for enabled providers by using this.getProviders() as in the original implementation.

issues.title: Empty suffix array incorrectly bypasses generic calendar filtering
issues.description: The filtering logic adds a length check (genericCalendarSuffixes?.length) that treats an empty array as falsy, setting AND to undefined instead of an empty array. In Prisma, AND: undefined means no filtering, while AND: [] also means no filtering but with different semantics. More critically, this breaks the filtering for providers like office365_calendar that have an empty suffix list in GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES. The double optional chaining (?. used twice) is redundant and the length check changes the behavior from the intended design where empty arrays should still be processed.

issues.title: Incomplete class rename breaks all imports and causes runtime failures
issues.description: The class was renamed from SelectedCalendarRepository to PrismaSelectedCalendarRepository (line 5) without providing a backward-compatible export alias. This breaks all existing code that imports this class. The test file within this PR (SelectedCalendarRepository.test.ts:2,50,53) still imports and instantiates the old class name, causing test failures. Production code in apps/web/app/api/cron/calendar-subscriptions/route.ts:41 and apps/web/app/api/webhooks/calendar-subscription/[provider]/route.ts:61 also use 'new SelectedCalendarRepository(prisma)' which will fail at runtime with a TypeError indicating SelectedCalendarRepository is not a constructor.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #26774 - feat: CalendarCache - filter generic calendars from subscription batch

structured_output.summary:
This PR stops the calendar-subscription cron from picking up Google's "generic" calendars (holidays, contacts, imported, resource). It adds a `GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES` map and a `getGenericCalendarSuffixes()` method to the adapter factory. `CalendarSubscriptionService.checkForNewSubscriptions` passes those suffixes to `findNextSubscriptionBatch`, and the repository turns each one into `AND: [{ NOT: { externalId: { endsWith } } }]`. The filter itself is correct: `externalId` is non-nullable, and `AND: undefined` is ignored by Prisma.

The PR also renames the exported class `SelectedCalendarRepository` to `PrismaSelectedCalendarRepository` without updating anything that uses it. Two production routes (the calendar-subscriptions cron and the calendar-subscription webhook) and the repository's own test file still import and construct `SelectedCalendarRepository` from this module. That breaks the type-check and build, and the tests the description says prove the change will fail to run. There's also a product question: `@group.calendar.google.com` covers user-created secondary calendars as well as shared ones.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The class rename isn't mentioned in the description, and it breaks the imports in two production API routes and the repository's test file, so the build fails. The filtering logic is sound once that's fixed.

architecture.overview:
The calendar-subscription feature uses a cron route (`/api/cron/calendar-subscriptions`) that builds a `CalendarSubscriptionService` from a `DefaultAdapterFactory`, a feature-flag repository and a `SelectedCalendarRepository`. `checkForNewSubscriptions` gets the teams that have the cache feature enabled. It then asks the repository for up to 100 selected calendars on the supported providers that have never been subscribed or whose channel has expired, and calls `subscribe()` on each one.

This PR makes the adapter factory the single place that lists generic-calendar `externalId` suffixes for each provider. The service passes the combined list to the repository, which excludes matching rows with Prisma `NOT endsWith` clauses. In the same change, the Prisma repository class is renamed to `PrismaSelectedCalendarRepository`.
steps: Start at `apps/web/app/api/cron/calendar-subscriptions/route.ts`: it constructs the service with `DefaultAdapterFactory` and the selected-calendar repository.

`AdaptersFactory.ts` now exports `GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES` (Google: group.v, group, import, resource; Office 365: empty) and `getGenericCalendarSuffixes()`, which flattens the suffixes for all providers.
`SelectedCalendarRepository.ts` adds an `AND` array of `NOT externalId endsWith <suffix>` clauses, or `undefined` when the list is empty, and renames the class to `PrismaSelectedCalendarRepository`.
The interface and the unit tests are updated to match the new optional parameter.

findings.title: Renaming the class to `PrismaSelectedCalendarRepository` breaks existing imports in two routes and the test
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/selectedCalendar/repositories/SelectedCalendarRepository.ts` line 5, the class was renamed from `SelectedCalendarRepository` to `PrismaSelectedCalendarRepository`, but `apps/web/app/api/cron/calendar-subscriptions/route.ts`, `apps/web/app/api/webhooks/calendar-subscription/[provider]/route.ts`, and `packages/features/selectedCalendar/repositories/SelectedCalendarRepository.test.ts` still import and instantiate `SelectedCalendarRepository`. The rename is unrelated to this feature, so revert the class name to `SelectedCalendarRepository`. If the rename is intentional, update every import and `new` call instead, and grep the repo to confirm nothing else imports the old name from this module. Then run the type-check and the repository tests.

findings.title: `@group.calendar.google.com` also matches user-created secondary calendars
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/calendar-subscription/adapters/AdaptersFactory.ts` lines 12-20, `GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES.google_calendar` includes `@group.calendar.google.com`. Google also uses that suffix for user-created secondary calendars, so they would never be subscribed or cached. Check whether that's intended. If not, remove the entry and keep `@group.v.calendar.google.com`, `@import.calendar.google.com` and `@resource.calendar.google.com`, then update the test fixtures in `CalendarSubscriptionService.test.ts`. If it is intended, extend the doc comment to explain why secondary or shared calendars are excluded.

findings.title: Redundant optional chaining, and suffixes include providers outside `getProviders()`
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/selectedCalendar/repositories/SelectedCalendarRepository.ts` lines 41-45, remove the redundant `?.` in `genericCalendarSuffixes?.map` because the ternary already checks `.length`. In `packages/features/calendar-subscription/adapters/AdaptersFactory.ts` `getGenericCalendarSuffixes()` (around line 67), consider replacing `Object.keys(...).flatMap` with a cast by `this.getProviders().flatMap((p) => GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES[p])` so the suffixes line up with the enabled providers.

findings.title: `DefaultAdapterFactory.getGenericCalendarSuffixes()` has no direct test
findings.fixPrompt: Add a unit test for `DefaultAdapterFactory.getGenericCalendarSuffixes()` in `packages/features/calendar-subscription/adapters/AdaptersFactory.ts` (lines 61-71) that checks it returns the flattened values of `GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES`. In `packages/features/calendar-subscription/lib/__tests__/CalendarSubscriptionService.test.ts`, replace the four repeated suffix arrays with a single shared constant, or import `GENERIC_CALENDAR_SUFFIXES.google_calendar`.

findings.title: The filter is safe at the query level
findings.body: `SelectedCalendar.externalId` is a non-nullable `String`, so `NOT endsWith` won't silently drop rows where the value is NULL. Prisma ignores `AND: undefined`, so callers that don't pass suffixes get exactly the old behavior. The new repository test checks the generated `where` clause directly. Filtering in the query also stops these calendars from being picked up again on every cron run, since a failed `subscribe()` never sets `syncSubscribedAt` and they would otherwise come back each time.
